lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is not needed to assess qualifications and adds personal information without helping the application.

items.says: Remove nationality unless the application requests it or it clarifies eligibility.
items.because: It is usually unnecessary and is not a substitute for work authorization.

items.says: Clarify whether the MBA is completed or in progress.
items.because: The listed end date alone may not make its status clear.

items.says: Clarify the baseline, measurement period and population behind the 35% figure.
items.because: The scope of the checkout-conversion result is unclear.

items.says: Reconcile “for all merchants” with the later pilot-region and opt-in descriptions.
items.because: The bullets may describe separate initiatives or overlapping work.

items.says: Make clear what you personally owned versus what the team delivered.
items.because: “The team shipped it” leaves your contribution unclear.

items.says: Clarify the currency of the 1.1 million dollars.
Identify the annual loss figure as an estimate if that is how it was calculated.
Make sure the claim that the analysis set the roadmap priority is supportable.
Clarify what the onboarding tickets covered.
Clarify whether you closed the tickets or coordinated the team that did.
Give the starting point, endpoint and time period for the queue reduction.
items.because: Those details are needed to make the reduction clear.

items.says: Add a finding, or combine or remove the measurement bullet.
items.because: It describes an evaluation method but gives no result.

items.says: Avoid implying the redesign caused a difference based on the opt-in comparison alone.
items.because: Merchants chose their own flow.

items.says: Clarify the pilot period and how the median time was measured.
Distinguish the onboarding result from checkout conversion, or avoid listing overlapping work as separate accomplishments.
items.because: The claims may describe the same initiative with different scopes or metrics.

items.says: Avoid presenting the before-and-after change as proven causal unless the analysis supports it.
Excluding weather-delayed shipments does not establish that late deliveries fell.
items.because: It changes the calculation and may reflect a reporting change rather than better delivery performance.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period or baseline for the 30% reduction.
Correct the present-tense “prepares.”
items.because: The role ended in 2023.

items.says: Add the outcome or scope of the S&OP work, or shorten or remove the bullet.
items.because: It currently gives no outcome beyond a routine responsibility.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,800 annual driver hours were measured savings or an estimate.
Clarify whether the driver-hour savings were achieved after rollout.
Distinguish students who could use the app from those who actually used it.
items.because: “Launched ... to 3,100 students” does not make that distinction clear.

items.says: Clarify how the nine-tonne figure was tracked or estimated.
Define the measurement periods for the weekly-active-user figures.
Avoid attributing the entire user increase to reminders without support.
items.because: The before-and-after figures alone may not establish that the reminders caused it.

items.says: Clarify the time period for the filled-slot and staff-cover figures.
Explain what “staff cover shifts” means.
items.because: Readers need that context to interpret the operational effect.

items.says: Add a substantiated outcome or deliverable, or remove the bullet.
items.because: Weekly sessions describe an activity rather than what changed because of the work.

items.says: Explain your role in mapping intake or shortening the form.
items.because: The passive construction obscures who did the work.

items.says: Clarify how many clinics adopted the changes.
Explain what the adoption changed.
items.because: The current wording does not show its effect.

items.says: Remove or correct the merchant-onboarding result under the hospital practicum.
items.because: It conflicts with the hospital context and duplicates the Harbor Payments result.

items.says: Prioritize product skills most relevant to the target role and supported by experience.
items.because: The experience section should substantiate the skills listed.
